title: Sleeman Centre operating model and youth discount
subtitle: Also: development charge by-law update, 2026 property tax ratios, recreation facility allocation and lobbyist registry review.
overview: The committee recommended moving the Sleeman Centre toward a more event-driven model. That includes more staff flexibility on rates and fees, a higher ticket service charge for the capital reserve fund, and an end to the youth rental discount at the Sleeman Centre only. The youth discount recommendation passed {{vote:m9}} after a motion to refer it to the March 31 Council meeting was defeated {{vote:m8}}. All three Sleeman clauses still go to Council at the end of the month.

The committee also recommended administrative updates to the development charge by-law to match provincial legislation, without changing rates. It recommended keeping 2026 property tax ratios unchanged, and it recommended approval of the recreation facilities allocation process. It received the lobbyist registry one-year review for information.

After a closed session, the committee reported that it gave direction to staff on the Guelph Storm Hockey Club operating agreement and on a corporate cybersecurity briefing. No further details were made public.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the youth facility discount no longer apply to rentals at the Sleeman Centre from September 1, 2026 {{vote:m9}}.

decisions.item: Sleeman Centre rates and ticket charge
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that staff may negotiate Sleeman Centre rates and fees where revenue can be recovered, and that the capital reserve ticket service charge rise to between $2.00 and $3.00 from September 1, 2026.

The committee recommended approving the 2026 development charges update study, the amending by-law and the updated interest policy, and directing staff to update the Local Service Policy by May 27, 2027.
The committee recommended keeping tax ratios for all classes, including multi-residential, unchanged and approving the 2026 ratios and tax rates.
The committee recommended approving the updated process for allocating recreation facilities to user groups.
The committee received the Lobbyist Registry One Year Review report for information.

debate: Staff said long September-to-March bookings limit the Sleeman Centre's ability to host concerts, film shoots and larger events. They argued that groups should be moved now, while new ice is being added at the South End Community Centre, and that no group would lose ice time.

Staff said youth groups moved to other arenas would keep their youth discount. They also noted the discount is not offered at River Run Centre, so the change would make the premier facilities consistent.

Several councillors wanted to defer the youth discount clause. They cited groups that had already set fees, non-ice youth events such as competitions and camps, and uncertainty about the South End opening. Staff agreed to provide a memo on how often the discount is used, and one councillor asked for monitoring of the transition. Others supported all three clauses as a cost-saving step after the property tax increase.

On development charges, staff said payment at occupancy creates cash flow pressure and likely more capital deferrals. They said exempting residential charges would shift costs to property taxes and water rates, and that the city cannot require savings to be passed on to buyers. A councillor suggested a letter asking the province for a pause in planning and charge changes.

On property tax, staff recommended waiting for provincial reassessment before changing the multi-residential ratio. Lowering it now would raise bills for other residential properties, and staff flagged that new multi-residential buildings will move into the higher class after 35 years.
